citation: Underwood & Underwood, "Begorrah, Bridget, lit's arbitrate", stereograph, copyright 1901. Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, LOT 3531-4, LC-USZ62-47713 (item 2006689888).
author: Underwood & Underwood
repository: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division; half-stereo copy negative LC-USZ62-47713, reference image 3a47865r.jpg read at tile.loc.gov.
locator: The single frame: a stout older woman cook standing at a kitchen table with a rolling pin raised, full length at about three metres, a man fallen against the dresser beside her.
rights_note: LOC rights advisory: 'No known restrictions on publication.' Published 1901. Used only as a reference picture the 1904 cook is judged against and for the cut of her working dress and apron (T-3479); nothing is traced or sampled from it.
access_notes: Viewed 2026-11-07 (T-3479) from the LOC reference image; the catalogue marks its caption-card data 'unverified, old data'. A comic stereograph of the Irish cook the period's humour called 'Bridget': a stout older woman in a long dress of a large figured print with full long sleeves, a broad checked apron from the waist to near the hem wrapping round the skirt, black shoes, her hair drawn up. It is a caricature; only her working dress is read here, not her face, her figure or the joke.
note: A reference picture for the 1904 cook's dress, Kate Ryan of the Glessner household (data/humans/recipes/cook_1904.json).
what_it_supplies: an older working cook's long print dress with full sleeves and a broad checked apron wrapping round the skirt, about 1901
what_it_does_not_supply: anything about Chicago, the Glessner household or Kate Ryan; no likeness is asserted, and the picture is a caricature
